subject: DPA: deletion certification + backup retention negotiation
messages:
From: Laura Gibson <laura.gibson@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Harper <ben.harper@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-03 09:14 PDT
Subject: DPA questions: deletion cert + backups

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the draft DPA. Our legal/compliance team had a few focused questions on deletion and data residency we need resolved before procurement will move forward:

1) Deletion vs backups: the current redline says "delete within a commercially reasonable timeframe". For healthcare data we need concrete timelines. Can Redwood confirm: primary data deletion within 30 days of request, and a maximum backup retention/restore window we can rely on (we usually ask for <=90 days).

2) Certification: we require a deletion attestation (signed) confirming data expunged from primary stores, caches (KV, prefix caches), and backups. Will Redwood provide a "Certificate of Secure Erasure"? If so, what is the issuance SLA after a verified request?

3) Onshore/EU processing: we need assurance that all processing and logs for Acme Health will remain in EU regions. Are log exports, diagnostic traces, and backup copies kept onshore by default, or do you offer an onshore-only option?

4) Training/derivative use: please confirm that customer data will not be used to improve model weights or training datasets unless explicitly contracted.

Attached are the specific redline clauses our counsel proposed. We can be flexible but want concrete language on timelines and the deletion certification. Looping Ben (procurement).

Best,
Laura

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: DPA questions: deletion cert + backups

Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary and two options we can propose in the redline to keep momentum:

Summary of our positions:
- No training/weight updates with customer data unless explicitly agreed (we will add a permissive clause to that effect).
- We support EU-hosted processing and can lock processing + primary logs to the EU region for this account.
- Backups and disaster recovery copies are retained for operational resiliency; we can set an upper retention bound.

Two compromise proposals for your team to review (we'll incorporate whichever you prefer into the DPA redline):

Option A (faster attestation, longer backup window):
- Primary data deleted and made unrecoverable within 30 days of a valid request.
- Backups retained for up to 180 days for disaster recovery; data in backups is marked for deletion immediately after the request and inaccessible to restore outside of a documented process.
- Certificate of Secure Erasure issued within 45 days after completion of the deletion process.

Option B (shorter backup window):
- Primary deletion within 30 days.
- Backups purged in full within 90 days.
- Certificate of Secure Erasure issued within 30 days after deletion.

I'll pull neha and Vivek into this thread for the technical/legal details on how the deletion/backup flows and the attestation would work. Attached: our annotated redline + a short backup deletion spec that describes logical deletion vs physical media lifecycle.

Can you confirm which option Acme prefers, or share a counter? If you want, we can draft final language via DocuSign for sign-off.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_Redline_v2.pdf (redline), BackupDeletion-Specs.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Gibson <laura.gibson@acmehealth.com>, Ben Harper <ben.harper@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-04 08:37 PDT
Subject: Re: DPA questions: deletion cert + backups

Kimberly / team —

Technical/legal notes to support negotiation:

1) Primary data and caches: Redwood will implement immediate logical deletion of all primary customer data and associated prefix/KV caches upon validated request. Logical deletion means records are removed from indexes and made inaccessible; the underlying storage blocks are scheduled for secure overwrite per media lifecycle. For most object stores this results in logical deletion within minutes and physical overwrite on subsequent garbage collection cycles.

2) Backups: our standard DR backups are immutable snapshots stored encrypted. We can commit to an upper bound retention window in the DPA. Operationally: when a deletion request is received we will (a) mark the customer dataset in the backup index as ineligible for restore, (b) queue any affected snapshots for secure purge, and (c) complete purge within the agreed backup retention window. For on-prem/tape media the physical destruction timeline will follow our media retirement SOP.

3) Attestation: Redwood can provide a "Certificate of Secure Erasure" that includes: the scope of data erased, the systems affected, timestamps, and an operator signature. Suggested SLA: issue certificate within 30–45 days depending on backup window (30 days if backups <=90d; 45 days if backups up to 180d). We cannot feasibly certify immediate physical overwrite for all legacy snapshots instantaneously, but the certificate will reflect the steps taken and final purge date.

4) EU residency: we can enable EU-only processing for your account and restrict log exports and support traces to EU regions. Note: some support diagnostic tasks may need temporary access; we can require explicit approval for any cross-border debug activities and log exports.

5) No training: confirm clause prohibiting any use of customer-originated data for training or model improvement unless a separate agreement exists. We'll add explicit language.

I'll attach the internal backup purge flow and the sample certificate template to the redline. If Acme pushes for a 30-day certificate and 90-day backup purge, we can accept that with the caveat that certain legacy immutable snapshots may require media-retirement timelines which we'll include in the certificate.

-Neha
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Neha —

Thanks for the detailed options and the transparency on the operational constraints. Acme's preferred baseline is:

- Primary data: deletion within 30 days.
- Backups: full purge within 90 days; if any legacy immutable media prevents a 90-day physical overwrite, you must disclose that in the certificate and provide a documented remediation plan with target dates.
- Certificate: issued within 30 days of the final purge with operator signature and scope.
- EU residency: yes, we need EU-only processing and logs retained only in EU regions, no cross-border debug without written approval.

If Redwood can accept those four points in hard language, procurement will sign the DPA immediately. I'll ask procurement Ben Harper to look out for a DocuSign.

-Best,
Laura

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Laura Gibson <laura.gibson@acmehealth.com>, Ben Harper <ben.harper@acmehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-06 15:22 PDT
Subject: Re: DPA questions: deletion cert + backups

Laura / Ben —

Thanks — we can accept Acme's baseline with the following final DPA language we will insert:

1) Deletion: "Redwood will, upon a verified deletion request, make customer data inaccessible and remove records from primary stores within thirty (30) days."

2) Backups: "Redwood will mark backups as ineligible for restore immediately upon request and will complete secure purge of backups within ninety (90) days, except where immutable media or legal holds require a longer timeframe; any such exceptions will be disclosed in the Certificate of Secure Erasure and accompanied by a remediation plan with target dates."

3) Certificate: "Redwood will issue a Certificate of Secure Erasure within thirty (30) days following the completion of the purge described above. The certificate will include scope, systems, timestamps, and an authorized signature."

4) Residency: "Redwood will provision Acme Health's account in EU-only regions and will restrict logs, diagnostic traces, and backups to EU data centers unless Acme provides prior written consent for cross-border exports."

5) Training: "Redwood will not use customer data for model training or to improve model weights unless a separate written agreement is executed."

I've updated the redline with these clauses and created a DocuSign envelope for the DPA. Link: https://app.docusign.com/someDocId/ABCDEFG. I've attached the final redline (DPA_Redline_v2.pdf) and the backup deletion spec for your records. Please route to Ben for signature and let me know if you want any minor edits — we should be able to finalize within 48 hours of signature.

Thanks,
